task.description: Write test spec and test code for REQ-036. This has real application-executable surface (3 new pure/read-only Elixir modules) -- the scope-test skip does not apply, proceed with the full procedure. Read REQ-036's 6 acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml, the validated design at lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md, and the 3 implementation files. Write test/specs/REQ-036.md (requirement text, test cases, why each exists) and test code under test/letflow/definitions/ (promotion_plan_test.exs, promotion_conflict_test.exs, promotion_digest_test.exs), following this codebase's existing fixture/tenant-schema-per-test convention (see test/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store_test.exs or graph_test.exs for precedent on setting up per-test tenant schemas via TenantProvisioning). Since compute_promotion_plan/5 requires opts[:permission_checker] (Keyword.fetch! -- no default, raises if omitted), every test calling it must inject one explicitly (a deterministic fn returning true/false as the test needs). For AC3 (production-tenant rejection), you must inject opts[:tenant_classifier] explicitly since the real default classifies everything :test (design sec 9.2) -- there is no way to construct a real production-tenant fixture against the current schema, this is expected, not a gap in your test design. Cover REQ-036's 6 acceptance criteria as a floor, plus the two flagged edge cases from the design (sec 9.4: version_greater?/2's numeric-vs-lexicographic fallback -- test both an all-numeric-version pair and a non-numeric-version pair explicitly) and PromotionDigest's AC5 in at least two independently-constructed differently-key-ordered plans (not just one nested example). Also test PromotionConflict's list-length-mismatch guard clause and the zero-conflicts/multiple-conflicts cases.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-036's 6 acceptance criteria has at least one runnable ExUnit test that would fail if the behavior were violated
version_greater?/2's numeric and non-numeric (lexicographic fallback) cases both explicitly covered by a test, per design sec 9.4
compute_plan_digest/1's key-order-independence covered by at least 2 independently-constructed differently-ordered examples, not 1
Every compute_promotion_plan/5 test call supplies opts[:permission_checker] explicitly (no reliance on a nonexistent default)
Test fixtures use per-test unique tenant/data (no shared hardcoded IDs), matching this codebase's established tenant-isolation test convention
No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
test/specs/REQ-036.md written alongside the test code, not as an afterthought
